EBITDA $76M (25.2%); FY26 bookings $1,285M, revenue $1,207M, adj. EBITDA margin 26.5%. MarketBeat consensus EPS $0.569 / revenue $303.22M (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-11-3-duolingo-inc-stock/); Earnings Whispers EPS $0.55, whisper $0.52 (finviz preview 2026-10-26). The bar is sourced to the company guide plus agreeing estimate sources. print_vs_bar_pct is measured against about $304M consensus revenue / $309M bookings.
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 7,103,345 shares at the 2026-10-15 FINRA settlement (prior 7,152,857), 8.47 days to cover on 839k ADV, about 15.2% of the 46.79M Class A shares outstanding (equibles, https://equibles.com/stocks/duol/shortinterest). A separate aggregator showed 7.15M shares / 6.7 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement. This is a crowded short, so negatives were shrunk. The 25-delta skew was rejected by the baseline (46.5 vol points flagged implausible), so there is no usable directional skew. Put/call OI is 0.75 (call-heavy). ATM IV is 167.6%; event-implied move 13.54%. The stock is down 8.6% over 20 days, 4.2% over 5 days, about 15% from about $159 on 2026-09-01, and 49% below its 52-week high.

evidence.text: Third-party DAU tracking points to Q3 DAU growth at or slightly above the 63.49M (+25.7%) consensus. D.A. Davidson's panel of over 170k users implied Q3 DAU growth of 25.6-27.6% y/y (August DAUs +1.3% m/m), against 23% in Q2 and a company FY assumption of about 20%. A 2026-11-03 Investing.com preview says unnamed analysts' proprietary data show October trends pointing to further DAU acceleration, which could prompt a DAU guide raise.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-05): DAUs accelerated to +23% and beat the company's expectations; the stock fell 9.41% on a moderate revenue guide. Q3 2025 (2025-11-05): DAUs +36%; the stock fell 25.49% when management prioritised users over monetization. This name has sold DAU beats.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The 63.49M DAU consensus (+25.7%) already sits inside the panel range, so only the top half of that range (above about 26%) and any October acceleration feeding a raised DAU guide would be news. If the market were paying for the DAU tracking, the stock would not be down about 15% since the Sep 1-2 upgrades.
evidence.independence: Investing.com preview 2026-11-03 (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/duolingo-earnings-on-deck-can-user-growth-justify-margin-tradeoff-93CH-4926363) cites October proprietary data pointing to acceleration. The 2026-08-18 D.A. Davidson upgrade (https://pro.edgex.exchange/en-US/news/article/duolingo-stock-jumps-after-da-davidson-upgrade) said +24% from data through mid-August. Both rest on broker panels, not on company data.

evidence.text: On the Q2 call (2026-08-05) management disclosed a bonus plan that pays about $10M in cash, more if growth is higher, if Q4 2026 DAU growth reaches 25%; it is excluded from FY guidance. With tracking at 25.6-27.6% for Q3 and October reportedly accelerating, an accrual in Q3/Q4 is likely. That would push Q3 adj. EBITDA below the $76M guide and/or trim the FY 26.5% margin guide by about 0.8 points.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Margin guides were punished: the FY26 guide with a margin squeeze (2026-02-26) fell 14.01%, and the January 2026 preliminary print plus CFO exit fell 8.45%. The Q2 raise of the EBITDA margin outlook by nearly a point did not stop a 9.41% fall.
evidence.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The plan is public but excluded from guidance, and the EBITDA consensus has not been visibly cut (EPS consensus was revised down only 0.4% in 30 days per Zacks). If it were priced, Q3 EBITDA and EPS consensus would sit about $5M under the company's $76M guide.
evidence.independence: Investing.com preview 2026-11-03 (https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/duolingo-earnings-on-deck-can-user-growth-justify-margin-tradeoff-93CH-4926363) independently says the bonus would be recognised in Q3 and Q4 and temporarily depress EBITDA margins. That preview shares the DAU-tracking premise with finding 1, so this finding is the same DAU strength read through its cost. The two are sized for opposite effects and do not double-count.

evidence.text: Monetization lags users, which is a risk to the Q4 bookings guide. Q3 bookings were guided to only +8.9% ($307M, consensus $309.05M) and FY bookings were not raised despite DAU acceleration. In August the CEO said Max might be sunset, and a 'Super Lite' tier at about half Super's price (ads, limited Energy; $35.99/yr seen on iPhone 2026-09-06) was in test. Both are ARPU / mix headwinds to bookings per DAU going into the Q4 and 2027 outlook.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Every one of the last five reactions (-9.41, -5.62, -14.01, -8.45, -25.49) followed a release where bookings or revenue guidance, or a monetization trade-off, disappointed while users were fine.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The guide is public and the stock is 49% off its high, so this finding rests on the tier test and the Max decision not being reflected in the Q4 bookings consensus. If the market expected an ARPU hit, bookings consensus would be at or below guide rather than $2M above it.
evidence.independence: The Max-sunset / Super Lite reporting is from a review site summary of the CEO's Q2 call comments (search result 'Language App Guide', checked 2026-09-06) and was not verified against the transcript. The finviz/Earnings Whispers preview of 2026-10-26 (https://finviz.com/news/408330/duolingos-user-rebound-faces-a-test-can-q3-show-bookings-catching-up-to-daus) frames the same bookings-vs-DAU gap.

evidence.text: On 2026-09-03/04 Duolingo and Bharti Airtel announced 12 months of Super Duolingo free for Airtel's roughly 376M Indian subscribers, activated in the Airtel Thanks app with no card. This is likely a September-onward DAU and possibly paid-subscriber lift in India at low or unknown ARPU.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior telco bundle; India is a low-ARPU market. DAU lines have not been rewarded (see finding 1).
evidence.why_not_priced: The deal's economics (wholesale fee or not, whether bundle users count as paid subscribers) are undisclosed, so neither consensus subs (13.12M) nor bookings can reflect it. If priced, the paid-sub consensus would show a step-up beyond trend.
evidence.independence: indiantelevision.com (https://indiantelevision.com/iworld/duolingo-partners-with-airtel-to-give-subscribers-a-free-12-month-super-duolingo-subscription/) reports the same deal. This is a proxy: the company has not quantified any impact.

evidence.text: FX: Q3 guidance was set at July 31 rates, and the company says each 1% move in the dollar is worth about $4M of H2 bookings. The DXY fell from about 100.35 (end July) to 99.55 (end August) and was roughly flat over the quarter; USD/JPY fell 3.2% in Q3, and Japan is a large market. That gives a small Q3 bookings tailwind of about $1-2M. A reported October dollar rebound would be a small headwind to the Q4 guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No record of FX driving a reaction on this name.
evidence.why_not_priced: Too small to matter. It would show up as a $1-2M bookings beat inside normal guide conservatism.
evidence.independence: NAGA Q3 review (https://naga.com/za/news-and-analysis/articles/forex-market-outlook): DXY +0.2% over Q3, USD/JPY -3.2%. FX sensitivity is from the Q2 letter. Macro-to-company proxy.

evidence.text: Crowded short into the print: 7.10M shares short (about 15.2% of Class A shares outstanding) and 8.47 days to cover at the 2026-10-15 settlement. With the stock about 15% below its early-September level and 49% off its high, a print without a guide cut has squeeze fuel.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest peaked at 8.73M at the 2026-02-27 settlement, right after a -14.01% print, so shorts were paid on the last cycle. The only up reactions in eight prints (+21.61 May 2025, +13.75 Aug 2025) came when guidance surprised up.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is positioning itself, a mechanism rather than a fact. It is priced only to the extent the call-heavy OI (put/call 0.75) and 167% ATM IV already embed squeeze risk.
evidence.independence: Massive.com reported 7.15M short / 6.7 days at the 2026-09-30 settlement (https://massive.com/quote/duol).

evidence.text: CEO Luis von Ahn sold about 226,000 shares (about $34M) at $150-152 between 2026-09-16 and 2026-10-07 under a 10b5-1 plan, cutting direct holdings to about 5k shares (trust holdings not shown). The General Counsel and a director also sold in September. There were no open-market buys in Aug-Nov.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public Form 4s on pre-arranged plans carry little information, so this is near zero by construction.
evidence.independence: capital.com Form 4 summaries (https://capital.com/en-gb/news/duolingo-ceo-luis-von-ahn-disposes-of-usd-6-95-million) report the same filings.

evidence.text: Marqeta has beaten its own quarterly revenue guide: Q2 2026 net revenue grew 17% ($176.0M) against a 14-16% guide, and adjusted EBITDA grew 31%. The Q3 guide is 6-8% (about $173.1-176.4M), so a repeat beat of 1-3 points puts Q3 at roughly 8-10%, or $176-180M. That is about +1.5% against the guide midpoint and at or slightly above the $175.1M Benzinga consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat its revenue guide and the stock fell 7.13%. Q1 2026 (19% growth) fell 7.7% and Q4 2025 fell 7.21%. Earlier beats in 2025 rose 8.9-21%. The last three beats were sold.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. Consensus already sits at or above the guide midpoint, and a habitual beater's beat is expected. The Q3 figure itself is unseen. If the market expected a large beat, consensus would sit near $180M on every source, not split between $175M and $180M.
evidence.independence: The Q1 2026 release (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001522540/000152254026000036/mqearningsrelease-q1x2026.htm) shows 19% Q1 growth. The FY revenue guide was narrowed from 12-14% to 12-13% in August, which partly argues against a large beat.

evidence.text: The forward line is the Cash App issuance shift. Management said new Cash App issuance began declining in mid-June and expects little to no new issuance by year end. The Cash App drag in 2027 will be 'a little bit more' than the about 2 points expected for 2026. Q4 should show 'similar trends' to Q3. The FY 12-13% guide implies Q4 net revenue growth of only about 6.6-10.2%. Block was 41% of Q2 net revenue, and Q4 guidance plus any 2027 color is due on this call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Each of the last three prints carried a decelerating forward guide and fell 7.1-7.7% (2026-08-04, 2026-05-05, 2026-02-24). Q2's guide to 6-8% Q3 growth came with -7.13%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The deceleration itself is public. Not priced is the size of the 2027 step-down, which management declined to quantify ('details in early 2027'). Whether Q4 is guided to the low end of the implied 6.6-10.2% is also open. The 11.6% 20-day run-up toward the 52-week high is not what a market bracing for another step-down would show.
evidence.independence: eMarketer on the same call (https://www.emarketer.com/content/marqeta-will-issue--little-no--new-cash-app-cards-by-year-end). Same document, not independent. Block's own Q2 letter shows Cash App Commerce Enablement volume +17%, driven by Cash App Card (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001512673/000119312526335117/d91486dex991.htm). That supports the existing Block card base on Marqeta, which offsets part of this.

evidence.text: Klarna, a Marqeta customer since 2018 for US virtual cards and the Klarna Card, reported 6.5M Klarna Card active users at Q2 2026, up from 1.3M a year earlier. It also cut FY GMV guidance to $149-151B and guided Q3 GMV to $35-36B, with late-Q2 softness continuing into Q3. Marqeta's lending/BNPL TPV slowed from about 60% to over 40% in Q2, and it guided over 30% for H2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No line-specific history. BNPL is 1-2 points of Marqeta's guided Q3 deceleration.
evidence.why_not_priced: Klarna spoke two weeks after Marqeta's guide. Its card scaling (5x actives) is the part Marqeta processes and is not reflected in Marqeta's 30%+ H2 BNPL guide. Its GMV softness points the other way. It is a proxy with mixed sign, hence small.
evidence.independence: Marqeta powers the Klarna Card in the US and in 15 European markets (https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251103343270/en/Marqeta-Powers-Expansion-of-Klarna-Debit-Card-Across-Europe). Marqeta also disclosed that one BNPL customer is load-balancing virtual-card volume to other providers, which cuts against this.

evidence.text: DoorDash's Q3 2026 total orders grew 28% Y/Y to 993M and Marketplace GOV 36% to $33.9B, including Deliveroo. On-demand delivery is a Marqeta vertical that grew double digits in Q2 but below the company rate, with mix shifting to less favorable economics.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None specific. Management flagged a lower take rate in this vertical in Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: A peer printed after Marqeta last spoke. This is a sector proxy: no source here confirms which delivery platforms run on Marqeta, and the Deliveroo orders are largely non-US. Small.
evidence.independence: Marqeta's own Q2 call commentary on on-demand delivery (https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-8-3-marqeta-inc-stock/) says the take rate is falling, which partly offsets the volume.

evidence.text: Visa's calendar Q3 2026 payments volume grew 9% Y/Y in constant dollars, with cross-border +14%. Card spending was steady through the quarter Marqeta reports, consistent with Marqeta's 'not seeing a notable shift in spend or consumer behavior'.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Marqeta TPV has grown 32-33% against network volume near 9-10%, so macro explains little of its print.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced. It only rules out a macro-driven TPV miss. Macro proxy, not company-confirmed.
evidence.independence: none

evidence.text: Block (Marqeta's 41% customer) reports Q3 2026 the same evening after the close, with its call at 5:00 pm ET. Its Cash App Card and Commerce Enablement commentary lands inside the window, alongside Marqeta's own call at 4:30 pm ET.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No baseline history for coincident Block prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: The direction is unknowable before the release. Filed because it widens the reaction ([sizing note removed]. It carries no sign.
evidence.independence: The sweep row independently flags Block's same-evening print.

evidence.text: Positioning into the print: the stock is up 11.6% over 20 days and about 15% since mid-September (a director's 10b5-1 sale was at about $16.09 on 2026-09-16, now $18.47), 9% below its 52-week high. Short interest is a modest 5.04% of float with 4.6 days to cover, so there is no squeeze mechanism. The run-up raises the bar on a name whose last three beats were sold.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last three prints each fell about 7%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The run-up is the price itself. I found no news explaining the October rise, so the rally reads as positioning into an expected beat rather than repricing on a disclosed fact.
evidence.independence: Form 144 price reference: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1522540/000195004726009564/xsl144X01/primary_doc.xml (2026-09-16).

evidence.text: The board authorized a new $150M buyback on 2026-08-03 after exhausting the December 2025 program; $93.9M was repurchased in H1 2026. Q3 repurchase volume and share-count reduction will be disclosed in this print, on a market cap of about $4.2B.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The prior authorization did not prevent the -7% reactions.
evidence.why_not_priced: The authorization is public. The pace of Q3 use is not, and an aggressive pace would support per-share figures.
evidence.independence: Same 8-K as the Q2 release. Not independent.

evidence.text: Finance and governance turnover since the last print: the Chief Accounting Officer resigned effective 2026-08-21 with no successor named (the CFO takes over as principal accounting officer; the filing states 'not due to any disagreement'); a director resigned 2026-08-03; a new Chief Product Officer started 2026-08-31.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None.
evidence.why_not_priced: Small, quiet 8-Ks. Probably noise, and the filing explicitly disclaims any accounting disagreement.

evidence.text: DoorDash agreed on 2026-10-29 to acquire Instacart (Maplebear) for about $17B, closing end-2027 or H1 2028. Any consolidation of on-demand card programs for Marqeta would come long after this window, and I found no source tying either platform to Marqeta.
The 2027 Cash App run-rate drag ('a little bit more' than 2 points) will be quantified in early 2027, per management. Any partial color on this call is in the guidance finding.

evidence.text: Toast beat the top of its own recurring gross profit guide in each 2026 quarter: Q1 $529M against $505-515M (+2.7% above top) and Q2 $595M against $565-575M (+3.5% above top). The same beat on the Q3 guide of $615-625M would print about $635-645M (22-24% growth guided, about 26-28% implied). Q2 adjusted EBITDA was $221M against $185-195M, about $10M of it a tariff refund.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026 beat by $14M above the top of the guide and the stock fell -14.74% (the guide and hardware/tariff costs were blamed). Q2 2026 beat by $20M above the top and it rose +2.93%. Q4 2025 (Feb 2026) +4.55%, Q3 2025 +9.48%. Beats alone are not reliably paid.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: a beat of this size is the street's base case for a company that beats systematically. If the market expected no beat, the stock would not have run +11.8% into the print. What is not priced is a beat larger than about 3%.
evidence.independence: Q1 actual against guide comes from separate documents: the Q1 release https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001650164/000165016426000113/tost-20260331xexhibit991.htm (2026-05-07) and the Feb guide https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260212058106/en/Toast-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Year-2025-Financial-Results (2026-02-12). Census restaurant sales (separate finding) points the same way for GPV.

evidence.text: The FY2026 recurring GP guide ($2,325-2,355M) less Q1 ($529M), Q2 ($595M) and the Q3 guide ($615-625M) implies Q4 of about $576-616M, midpoint about $596M. That is about +19% on Q4 2025's $502M, against 22-24% guided for Q3 and 27-28% delivered in H1. If Q3 beats by about $20M and Q4 run-rates normally, an FY raise of $20-40M (about 1-2%) is arithmetically likely.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the guide. Q1 2026: FY raised, but a weak next-quarter guide and hardware cost uncertainty took it -14.74%. Q2 2026: FY raised by less than the beat (tariff refund reinvested), +2.93%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, so a modest raise is expected. A raise beyond the Q3 beat, putting implied Q4 at 22%+, would surprise. evidence.why_not_priced: A public macro series that sell-side can read, so partly priced. Transmission to Toast's SMB-weighted base is unconfirmed by the company. If priced as a sure GPV beat, the 20-day run-up would not sit next to a heavy put skew.

evidence.text: Insurance lead-gen peers that report after TREE beat Q3 guides set the same week as TREE's own (late July). EverQuote's Q3 revenue was $218.1m (+25% YoY) against a $198-208m guide (+7% vs the midpoint), with auto +21% and home/renters +70%. MediaAlpha's revenue was $375.9m (+23%) against a $330-355m guide (+10% vs the midpoint). Insurance was 67% of TREE's Q2 revenue ($209.3m, +42%). If TREE's insurance grew sequentially like EverQuote's auto line (+10.6% Q/Q), insurance would be about $231m, and total revenue would land above the top of TREE's $325-335m guide, against a $330.3m consensus sitting at the midpoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Insurance strength has not saved this stock. In Q2 2026 insurance revenue grew 42% and MediaAlpha beat consensus the same evening, yet TREE fell 19.6% on SMB weakness, a big adj EPS miss ($0.68 vs $1.41) and a lowered FY outlook. TREE's Q2 revenue of $313.4m missed the $315.6m consensus even though peers beat. The last 8 prints moved a median 20.9% in absolute terms.
evidence.why_not_priced: EverQuote reported last night, less than one session before TREE. TREE's consensus was not revised: it still sits at the $330m guide midpoint and drifted down from about $337m (EW 2026-10-26). If the street had priced the peer beats, revenue estimates would sit above the guide top. Part of the read may already be in today's +3.6% and the 20-day +13.6% run-up, which is why this is sized below the name's median move.
evidence.independence: MediaAlpha's Q3 8-K (2026-10-28, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000263/maxq32026-earningsreleasex.htm) points the same way: revenue $375.9m against a $330-355m guide, contribution $57.4m against $51.5-54.5m. Progressive's Q3 10-Q shows advertising up about 18% YoY to about $1.6bn, homeowners new applications +22% and personal-lines new applications slightly down (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000379/pgr-20260930.htm). These are peer and counterparty documents, not TREE's own number. Finding 2 rests on the same EverQuote and MediaAlpha releases, but on their Q4 lines.

evidence.text: The same peers' forward statements show carrier budgets still expanding into Q4. EverQuote guided Q4 revenue to $213-223m (midpoint about $218m) against a pre-report consensus of $211.9m, saying carriers 'continue to maintain strong underwriting profitability and an appetite for growth'. MediaAlpha guided Q4 revenue to $355-375m (+25% YoY at the midpoint) and said carriers are 'committing meaningful budgets in both home and auto insurance'. TREE's implied Q4 guide comes from FY2026 revenue of $1.30-1.32bn and VMM of $364-374m, which the street read as a cut in July. The peers' Q4 lines argue the insurance part of that implied Q4 is not at risk of a further cut and has room to be firmed.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is the line this stock traded on. In July a Q3 revenue guide 2% below consensus and a lowered FY outlook (EBITDA midpoint $148.5m vs $157.9m consensus) produced -19.6%. The April 2026 print was -21.7% and March was +23.9%. Moves of about 20% in either direction follow the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: TREE's Q4 consensus (about $339.5m revenue per one tracker) was set off July's guide cut and has not been revised since the peers spoke. If it had, Q4 estimates would have moved up after October 28 and November 2, and nothing shows that. SMB and consumer, not insurance, are the parts of TREE's guide the street doubts, so this lands on half of the guide question only.
evidence.independence: Shares documents with finding 1 (the EverQuote 8-K of 2026-11-02 at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001640428/000119312526443633/ever-ex99_1.htm and the MediaAlpha 8-K), read on their Q4 lines rather than their Q3 lines. Progressive's 10-Q shows ad spend still growing (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000080661/000008066126000379/pgr-20260930.htm). This is a proxy, not TREE's own guide.

evidence.text: SMB lender appetite stayed strong through Q3. Enova's small-business originations were about $1.8bn (+28% YoY, up from $1.6bn in Q2), and its SMB receivables were +34% YoY at 9/30. TREE's SMB weakness was the stated cause of the July drop. Its revised guide assumes lenders recover and merchants do not, and the CFO said lender appetite on the network 'has since stabilized'. Enova's growth supports the lender side of that assumption, not the merchant-demand side.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: This line drove the last print: weak SMB demand plus higher costs produced -19.6% on 2026-07-29. Consumer segment revenue was $60.3m in Q2 (-4% YoY), against $66.2m in Q3 2025.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Earnings Whispers preview (2026-10-26) frames SMB as the open question and says the market 'has leaned toward a longer slowdown'. A market pricing SMB recovery would not have the stock sitting near its post-earnings low. This is a proxy for one input, the lender side. The $1.8bn segment figure comes from a transcript summary; the primary release confirms only the +34% receivables growth.
evidence.independence: TREE's own Q2 8-K says lender appetite stabilised after the quarter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001434621/000162828026050633/tree-63026xer.htm). Earnings Whispers reports management calling July the best sales month since Q1. This is a lender-side proxy only; nothing found measures merchant demand.

evidence.text: Peer unit economics held or improved in Q3, which argues against TREE's insurance VMM squeeze getting worse. TREE's VMM fell to 28% of revenue in Q2 from 33%, blamed on Google traffic costs and carrier competition. EverQuote's variable marketing dollars were $62.6m on $218.1m revenue (28.7%), against a guide-implied 28.3%. MediaAlpha's contribution margin rose to 15.3% from 14.9% YoY, with contribution of $57.4m above its $51.5-54.5m guide.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In July, VMM up only 4% on revenue up 25%, together with a lower FY VMM range ($364-374m vs a prior $378-395m), was part of the -19.6% move.
evidence.why_not_priced: The preview names VMM margin as 'the more telling signal' and treats the squeeze as ongoing. If peers' stable margins were priced, TREE would not still trade near its lows with the VMM guide unrevised. This is an inference across companies: TREE's squeeze may be company-specific (its traffic mix), so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Shares the EverQuote document with findings 1-2. MediaAlpha's contribution margin comes from a separate 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001818383/000181838326000263/maxq32026-earningsreleasex.htm). There is nothing TREE-specific.

evidence.text: Shorts built into the print. Short interest rose from 846k shares (08-14) to 1.05-1.11m (09-30/10-15), and days to cover rose from 1.48 to 4.25, while the stock rallied about 19% off its $23.50 low to $28.07. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior squeeze episode on record for TREE prints. The +22.5% to +23.9% up-moves (2025-03, 2025-07, 2026-03) show the stock can gap 20% or more on a good guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price, not a fact outside it. It enters as asymmetry: a 4.25 days-to-cover short base on a $394m cap amplifies a positive surprise more than a negative one. The sign is genuinely two-way, because rising shorts can also be informed selling, so the size is small.
evidence.independence: stockanalysis.com statistics (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/TREE/statistics/, updated 2026-11-03) show 1.05m short, 7.81% of float and a 3.27-day ratio.

evidence.text: There is balance-sheet room for a capital-return announcement. Net leverage fell to 1.9x and free cash flow is about $80m a year (EW preview), against a market cap of about $394m. evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: No buyback announcement in the last 8 prints, so there is no history on this line.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is an inference from a sourced balance sheet, not a sourced intention. An implied 20% FCF yield on a stock 59% off its high suggests the market is not crediting capital return. If the market expected a buyback, the preview and the analysts would be discussing one.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: August 2026: the Q3 guide of $137-139m was below the $139.1-141.3m consensus and the stock still rose 9.54% on the beat. May 2026: the Q2 guide plus a margin hedge brought -11.83%. February 2026: the Q1 guide of $112-114m alongside a Q4 miss brought -6.86%.
evidence.why_not_priced: Consensus at $132.9m implies 8.7% growth, the same as the ex-China organic rate, which only works if China holds flat in a market down 20-28%. If the lap were priced, Q4 consensus would sit near $130m. This is my arithmetic, not a company statement, so it is sized small.
evidence.independence: The Q2 2026 regional table (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001767258/000176725826000071/xpelq22026earnings.htm) supplies the ex-China growth rate. It shares the China-market premise with the Eastman/CPCA finding, but this one lands on the guide and that one on the quarter.

evidence.text: US new-vehicle demand softened late in the quarter: September SAAR was 16.0m, down 3.5% month on month and 3.7% year on year, and Edmunds forecast Q3 volume 0.7% below Q3 2025. The US was 55% of XPEL revenue and grew 11.7% in Q2 against a roughly flat market, and the CEO cited continued dealership challenges ('FTC concerns').
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The US grew double digits through a flat SAAR in 2025-26, and the market has not traded XPEL on SAAR prints.
evidence.why_not_priced: Barely unpriced: SAAR is public. It is a macro-to-company proxy that XPEL has repeatedly outgrown, hence the small size.
evidence.independence: Edmunds Q3 forecast: https://www.edmunds.com/press/new-vehicle-sales-expected-to-dip-slightly-in-q3-amid-economic-headwinds-according-to-edmunds.html . Proxy only; XPEL has not confirmed it.

evidence.text: Tesla, an OEM and aftermarket channel for XPEL, delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026. That beat Tesla's compiled consensus of 461,974 but was about 2% below the 497,099 of Q3 2025, a quarter flattered by the US tax-credit pull-forward.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None recorded. Tesla was not mentioned on XPEL's Q2 call.
evidence.why_not_priced: Public datapoint. XPEL's Tesla exposure is not disclosed, so it is a proxy and sized near zero.
evidence.independence: Tesla 8-K exhibit: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001318605/000162828026064366/exhibit991111111.htm (the same fact).

evidence.text: Eastman's 2026-10-29 remarks say the Middle East conflict escalated during Q3 and was its primary driver of sequential decline, with Gulf order-fulfilment problems. XPEL's India and Middle East region ($6.4m, -5% in Q2) was hit by vehicle shortages, but the Q3 guide explicitly assumed no recapture of that business.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Middle East vehicle shortages were cited around the May 2026 print (-11.83%) alongside the guide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely inside the guide, because management excluded recapture ('we're not expecting really any of that recapture', https://allmind.ai/earnings/event/2946562). Only a further decline below the Q2 run-rate is unpriced.
evidence.independence: Shares the Eastman document with the China finding. Separate Brent/Hormuz escalation coverage: https://www.businesstoday.com.my/2026/09/08/brent-hits-six-week-high-middle-east-conflict-escalates/

evidence.text: Short interest rose into the print: 10.72% of float and 13.2 days to cover at 2026-09-30 (up 4.65% on the prior report), against 8.85% and 11.7 days in August, while the stock sits 22% below its 52-week high.
evidence.source_date: 2026-09-30 settlement (via search snippet; page returned 403 to fetch)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After Q2 the shares rose 9.54% on a beat that came with a below-consensus guide, which fits short covering into a beat.
evidence.why_not_priced: Positioning is the bet, not information. It asymmetrically amplifies a beat (13 days to cover on 187k average daily volume), and this raises the upside tail more than the mean.
evidence.independence: Equibles August figure: https://equibles.com/stocks/xpel/shortinterest
